summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and amiodarone-induced hyperthyroidism was admitted after developing left-sided chest pain, shortness of breath, and bilateral hand cramping immediately following a dialysis session. Initial concerns included air embolism and acute coronary syndrome, but serial cardiac enzymes and EKGs were negative, and chest imaging showed resolution of prior pulmonary edema without new acute findings. Symptoms resolved within hours, and he remained stable on telemetry with controlled heart rate on diltiazem. Potassium levels fluctuated but were managed medically. Cocaine use was noted as a complicating factor, contraindicating beta-blocker use. He was discharged home with instructions to continue dialysis on his regular schedule, monitor for recurrent chest pain, and follow up with cardiology, nephrology, endocrinology, and primary care. Medication adjustments included switching to 90 mg daily cinacalcet and 81 mg chewable aspirin, with continued home therapies for heart failure, diabetes, and hyperthyroidism.
